summary: INNER JOIN combines rows from two tables wherever a condition matches.
points: FROM a JOIN b ON a.key = b.other_key is the usual form. JOIN means INNER JOIN.
Rows with no match on either side are left out.
Short aliases keep queries readable: FROM orders o JOIN customers c.
Prefix column names with the table when both tables have a column of that name.

example.explanation: Each order finds its customer through customer_id. Noor has no orders, so she doesn't appear.
